rules.reason: the extension and its server integrate only through shared/ (the vendored single-source of categories/normalizeUrl) and the HTTP contract — never by referencing each other's code

accept.reason: the server's deploy/OAuth guide documents how the two halves relate (the extension manifest key, config.mjs client id, `cd ../extension` build) — cross-cutting setup docs, not a code coupling; the server ships no import of extension code
a comment notes the server must allow X-Client-Version in CORS (template.yaml AllowHeaders) — documentation of the HTTP contract, not a code reference into server/
orientation prose only — the router names where the vendored canon lives so a reader knows the guidance is injected, not authored here; no code or content in this repo depends on the path

same orientation pointer — the working-instructions router says the general discipline is auto-injected from the vendored corpus rather than restated here, which is the sentence that stops the doc duplicating canon prose

sharedConstants.what: the extension version, carried in three JSON files that can't share an import: extension/manifest.json is the shipped, user-visible number; extension/package.json is the npm record the release config names as package_json_path; the repo-root package.json is what cer/version-sync reads by name. The daily auto-release bumps all three in one commit (the two release-config paths via .github/actions/bump-extension-patch, the root file via the align step in chrome-extension-daily-release.yml), so any disagreement here means a bump landed in some files but not all
